items.descriptionAdvanced: Mount Assiniboine, standing at 3,618 meters, is often called the 'Matterhorn of the Rockies' due to its spectacular pyramidal silhouette. Located on the border between British Columbia and Alberta, this peak is one of the most iconic landmarks in the Canadian Rockies. The Mount Assiniboine Provincial Park has protected this fragile alpine ecosystem since 1922. The area is renowned for its glacial lakes, such as Lake Magog, which serves as a base for many hiking trails. Geography K7 — mountains and glaciers.
factsAdvanced: Elevation of 3,618 meters.
Named by George Mercer Dawson in 1885.
Situated on the border of British Columbia and Alberta.
Lake Magog is the primary base for hikers.
Its pyramidal shape was carved by glacial erosion.
The park was established in 1922.

items.descriptionAdvanced: The South Nahanni River flows through Nahanni National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage site in the Northwest Territories. This waterway is famous for Virginia Falls, which has a 96-meter drop, significantly taller than Niagara Falls. The region is characterized by deep canyons, karst cave systems, and unique hot springs. The river is a top destination for adventurers and rafting enthusiasts, offering a wild and nearly untouched landscape in Canada's far north. Geography K7 — rivers and waterfalls.
factsAdvanced: Virginia Falls has a 96-meter drop.
The river is approximately 540 kilometers long.
Included in the UNESCO World Heritage list in 1978.
Traditional territory of the Dene indigenous people.
Known for complex karst systems.
Nahanni National Park covers over 30,000 km².

items.descriptionAdvanced: Great Slave Lake is the second-largest lake in the Northwest Territories and holds the title of the deepest lake in North America, reaching a maximum depth of 614 meters. The city of Yellowknife, the territorial capital, is located on the lake's northern shore, having grown rapidly during the gold rush of the 1930s. During winter, the lake's frozen surface allows for the formation of ice roads essential for transport between isolated communities. Its clear water supports a rich biodiversity, essential for the regional ecosystem. Geography K7 — hydrology and lakes.
factsAdvanced: Maximum depth of 614 meters.
Surface area of approximately 27,200 km².
Second largest lake in Canada.
Yellowknife is located on the northern shore.
Water drains through the Mackenzie River to the Arctic Ocean.
Ice road networks are created in winter.

items.descriptionAdvanced: The Haida Gwaii archipelago, located off the coast of British Columbia, is often nicknamed the 'Galapagos of the North' due to its unique biodiversity that evolved in isolation after the last ice age. The islands are the cultural heart of the Haida people, famous for their totem poles and historic villages protected as a World Heritage site. The oceanic climate promotes the growth of lush temperate rainforests. The region provides an essential habitat for numerous endemic species and preserves the deep connection of the Haida people with the environment. Geography K7 — islands and biodiversity.
factsAdvanced: The archipelago comprises over 150 islands.
Main islands are Graham and Moresby.
Haida people have lived here for millennia.
Gwaii Haanas National Park is located in the south.
Oceanic climate with abundant rainfall.
Hosts numerous endemic plant and animal species.

items.descriptionAdvanced: Pacific Rim National Park protects valuable temperate rainforests on the west coast of Vancouver Island. These forests are characterized by giant, ancient trees that provide an important ecological niche. A well-known feature is the Long Beach Unit, famous for its vast sandy beaches. The area is a center for the conservation of Sitka Spruce and Western Red Cedar, which thrive under the wet conditions. Hikers can use the famous West Coast Trail to experience this untouched nature. Geography K7 — forests and ecology.
factsAdvanced: Long Beach Unit is a major tourist attraction.
Sanctuary for monumental Sitka Spruce trees.
Western Red Cedars reach impressive dimensions here.
West Coast Trail is one of the world's most famous hiking trails.
The ecosystem is strongly influenced by the Pacific Ocean.
Center for the study of temperate rainforest ecology.
